subject: Tweaking ggplot2 plots, faster redraw or WSIWYG-style editing?

messages.author: 04d533d544a1a631
messages.subject: Tweaking ggplot2 plots, faster redraw or WSIWYG-style editing?
parts:
Often ggplot2 will immediately produce almost the plot that I want and only after much effort am I able to get a finished product. 

I often have a ggplot2 command at the end of a fairly expensive R script. The script accesses a large amount of data and rearranges the data inside the script but doesn't produce any new data. Simply drawing the plot from the ggplot command takes more than I want to wait if I'm making small tweaks.

If I'm unlikely to produce the plot again with different data I simply resort to Illustrator. For plots I'll produce again, I usually settle for what I have even though the changes that I'd like to make are very easy to express to another human.

My question in general is, what is a reasonably efficient workflow for getting a plot "just-so"?

Is there any way to edit a ggplot2 plot interactively and then produce an R command that would have produced that plot?

Alternatively, is there a way to quickly redraw a ggplot2 output if I'm only making small changes to the R command that produces the plot?

Thanks.

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Tweaking ggplot2 plots, faster redraw or WSIWYG-style editing?
parts:
I don't know of any GUI/WYSIWYG editing, but I also run into the same issues when I work with large data. The key for my work flow is that I sample the data, using `sample` to render quickly and then add all of the features I want, like coloring, faceting, labels, etc., before using the full data set. Sometimes the sampling needs to be a bit more complex to make sure I get all values of discrete variable, but that takes much less time to do than watching a plot render with the full data. 

Also, I make strong use of the `+` operator as I add components. So I basically will do something like `p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)` and then play with it like, `p + ylab("Foo")` or `p + ylab("Bar")` to figure out what I want before committing the final plot, which would just be `p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y) + ylab("Foo")`. Once I have settled on everything, I kick off the "full" plotting and work on something else while in renders. I also use the `beepr` package's `beep` to give me an audio cue when it is done.

I'm not sure what I do is a great process, so I curious to hear from others.

Cheers,
Doug

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Tweaking ggplot2 plots, faster redraw or WSIWYG-style editing?
parts:
I have plotted some decently large datasets, but never so large that I have to wait more than a few seconds for it to plot so I usually just wait it out and iterate in the same way that Doug has suggested. Once you build a relatively reasonable code base I usually just copy and paste in what I think I need and then run it and see what breaks then iterate on that until I get what I want. 

I guess what I'm saying is that I don't have any fancy way of working either. Sampling a large dataset is a good idea if you are iterating a lot, but if you can do that you can also create a small reproducible dataset that has all of your factor levels and colors and whatnot that will plot in fractions of a second so you can iterate over scales, titles, labels, etc...

HTH, 
Brandon
